newsitem.title: MEXICO: Key facts about Mexico City mayor's election.
newsitem.headline: Key facts about Mexico City mayor's election.

text.p: This Sunday, residents of Mexico City, one of the world's biggest cities, will for the first time vote to elect a mayor. The post was previously filled by a presidential appointee.
Following are key facts about the election:

-- Population: metropolitan Mexico City sprawls across a huge area and contains around 17 million people. The election is being held in the Federal District, an enclave encompassing the central areas of the city which has 8.5 million people.
-- Federal District's budget: 34.37 billion pesos in 1997 ($4.3 billion).
-- Current mayor (the official title is Regent): Oscar Espinosa Villareal of the governing Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI).
-- The first elected mayor will serve three years beginning December 1997, subsequent mayors will serve six years.
-- The president retains the right to name the city's cheif of police and its chief prosecutor. The mayor cannot borrow money without his permission.
-- Eight candidates are fighting the election:
Main party candidates:
Alfredo del Mazo Gonzalez of the Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI) which has governed the capital since 1929
Cuauhtemoc Cardenas Solorzano of the left-wing Party of the Democratic Revolution (PRD)
Carlos Castillo Peraza of the conservative National Action Party (PAN)
Fringe party candidates:
Jorge Gonzalez Torres of the Green Ecologist Party of Mexico (PVEM)
Viola Trigo of the Workers Party (PT)
Baltazar Valadez Montoya of the Mexican Democratic Party (PDM)
Manuel Fernandez Flores of the Popular Socialist Party (PPS)
Pedro Ferriz Santacruz of the Cardenist Party (PC)
-- Voting begins at 8 a.m. local time (9 a.m. EDT) (1300 GMT) and ends at 6 p.m. (7 p.m. EDT) (2300 GMT).
-- Exit polls will start being released at 8 p.m. local (9 p.m. EDT) (0100 GMT Monday).
-- First results from the official preliminary count are expected from about 10 p.m. local (11 p.m. EDT) (0300 GMT Monday). Final official results will come Wednesday night or Thursday morning.
